# CLI command reference

Public API version: 1.0.0. Snapshot SHA-256: `965dcc0bd4ff8d803b9f3f54e86d385271c08f823eb07e85930135a87005d38f`.

Syntax and workflow notes come from the command registry. Request types, choices, defaults, bounds and descriptions come from the public contract.

## status

```text
storerouter status [--offline]

  Org, key, quotas, and whether onboarding worked

  Never mutates anything: no key minting, no file writes, no cache warming.
  Safe to run in a loop.

  `ok` is the single boolean to branch on, and it is true only when a key
  resolved, the API answered, and the organization is entitled. Exit 0
  healthy, 3 no usable credential, 4 not entitled, 5 throttled, 1
  unreachable.

  The probe is GET /v1/me, which requires a key and returns calling identity.

Options:
  --offline  Report local state only, with no network calls — for CI, and for 'is it me or the network?'.

Calls: getMe (through @octogen-ai/sdk 0.9.0)

Global options: storerouter --help
```

## skill

```text
storerouter skill [<reference>]

  Print the agent skill: how to use this CLI well

  Prints the agent skill bundled with this CLI version: when to use
  StoreRouter, which command fits a task, what each exit code means, and
  how to present results. With a path, prints a reference it links to.

  Piped output is the usual JSON envelope with the text in `markdown`;
  --no-json prints the Markdown itself. No network, no credential.

Global options: storerouter --help
```

## lookup

```text
storerouter lookup <url> [--match-mode …] [--resolution-mode …] [--on-demand-cache-policy …]

  Resolve one product URL to a product

  parse and lookup are one command: the same /products/lookup request and
  lookup JSON command.
  Exit 6 means the server looked and found nothing for this URL — which is
  not the same as the merchant being uncovered. Ask the coverage question
  by contacting StoreRouter about merchant coverage.

  Keyless-eligible, except --resolution-mode on_demand_only, which makes
  StoreRouter fetch the page and needs a key.

Options:
  --match-mode <strict|loose>                         Index match strictness. strict matches only exact/canonical URLs. loose (default) adds a lowest-priority fallback that ignores path case and query params, so a URL differing from an indexed product only by case (e.g. /Women/ vs /women/) or a non-indexed query param (e.g. Zara's ?v1=) still resolves. It also recognizes structural aliases: Shopify collection-scoped URLs (/collections/<x>/products/<handle>) resolve to the canonical /products/<handle> product. A strict/canonical hit always wins over a loose or alias one. Default: "loose".
  --on-demand-cache-policy <prefer_cache|refresh>     Cache behavior when the request enters the on-demand path. Default: "prefer_cache".
  --resolution-mode <auto|index_only|on_demand_only>  Source selection policy. auto checks the index before resolving on demand; index_only never performs outbound work; on_demand_only skips the index. Default: "auto".

Calls: lookupProduct (through @octogen-ai/sdk 0.9.0)

Global options: storerouter --help
```

## search

```text
storerouter search <query> [--catalog <key>] [--facet k=v]… [--price-min <n>] [--price-max <n>] [--limit <n>] [--cursor <c>]

  Search products by text

  Exit 6 means the corpus was searched and nothing matched — the answer was
  empty, not refused.

  The full search query object is deliberately not flagged; use
  `storerouter api POST /products/search` for it. Keyless-eligible.

Options:
  --catalog <value>  Catalog keys to search. Omit to search every catalog your key can access. Keys your key cannot access match nothing.
  --cursor <value>   `nextCursor` from the previous page, passed back verbatim with the same request body. Later pages reuse the understanding of `q` that page 1 ran rather than understanding it again.
  --facet <k=v>      Filters a product must match: every facet, and any value within a facet. A facet you send replaces any understood facet of the same name (a colour facet replaces both understood colour facets) and is never relaxed. Each name at most once.
  --limit <n>        Maximum results per page. Default: 50. Minimum: 1. Maximum: 100.
  --price-max <n>    Inclusive maximum price. Combined with any understood maximum by keeping the lower one. Minimum: 0.
  --price-min <n>    Inclusive minimum price. Combined with any understood minimum by keeping the higher one. Minimum: 0.

Calls: searchProducts (through @octogen-ai/sdk 0.9.0)

Global options: storerouter --help
```

## similar

```text
storerouter similar <url|uuid> [--catalog <key>] [--facet k=v]… [--no-relax] [--limit <n>]

  Find products similar to one you already have

  The source must be an indexed product: more-like-this does not resolve on
  demand. Exit 6 covers both 'the source is not indexed' and 'nothing was
  similar enough'; the `code` field separates them.

  Relaxation is on by default: a short first page is retried with the
  server's own generated facets dropped, never your --facet or price bounds.
  --no-relax turns it off.

  Requires an API key.

Options:
  --catalog <value>                      Optional catalog allowlist for the similar-products retrieval (breaking replacement for the former single-valued `catalog`). Restricts RESULTS to these catalogs only; source resolution is deliberately unrestricted so the source product may live outside the allowlist. Keys are not validated against the caller's grants — a key outside the caller's resolved scope simply matches nothing. When omitted, retrieval spans every catalog the caller's scope permits.
  --cursor <value>                       Opaque pagination cursor
  --exclude-facet <k=v>                  Filters a product must not match: products with any listed value of any listed facet are removed. Each name at most once.
  --facet <k=v>                          Filters a product must match: every facet, and any value within a facet. A facet you send replaces every generated facet of the same name (a `color` or `color_family` facet replaces generated facets on both colour axes); values are never unioned, and the other generated facets stay. Never relaxed. Each name at most once. Replaces `include_facets`, which is rejected.
  --limit <n>                            Limit Default: 12. Minimum: 1. Maximum: 100.
  --price-max <n>                        Inclusive maximum price. Combined with the `price_preference` bound by keeping the lower one. Minimum: 0.
  --price-min <n>                        Inclusive minimum price. Combined with the `price_preference` bound by keeping the higher one. Minimum: 0.
  --price-preference <lower|any|higher>  Relative price preference compared with the source product. Default: "any".
  --relax / --no-relax                   Retry with generated facets dropped in stages, least trusted first, when page 1 comes back short, and return the first stage that fills it. For a `uuid` or `url` source, and for `sources`, page 1 is short when it has fewer than `min(5, limit)` results and no `nextCursor`; a stage is adopted only if it reaches that floor, or any result for an empty page. For an `image` source, only an empty page 1 is relaxed. Facets and bounds you send are never dropped. The rule is the same as search's: what you send is never silently dropped, but the server may drop its own inferences. Here the generated facets are Platform's inference from the source product, not words you sent, so `relax` defaults to true; search defaults to false because its generated facets come from your `q`. A relaxed page's cursor continues the same relaxed results and is refused with `relax: false`. Default: true.

Calls: moreLikeThisProducts (through @octogen-ai/sdk 0.9.0)

Global options: storerouter --help
```

## store

```text
storerouter store <host|url>

  Show one store's coverage: catalogs, product counts, fields, prices

  Takes a bare host or any URL on the store, normalized the way the API
  normalizes hosts: lowercased, port and leading `www.` dropped. So
  `https://www.TheReformation.com/products/x` asks about thereformation.com.

  Exit 6 means the server answered 404 domain_not_covered: no catalog serves
  that host. One host per call; there is no list of covered hosts.

Calls: getDomain (through @octogen-ai/sdk 0.9.0)

Global options: storerouter --help
```

## brands search

```text
storerouter brands search <description> [--like <brand>]… [--facet k=v]… [--limit <n>]

  Find brands from a plain-language description

  Ranks brands by how well they match a plain-language description.
  --like names brands whose style steers the ranking; repeat it for several.
  Brand facets use the brand index's names, e.g. --facet facet_price_tier=premium.

  Exit 6 means the server searched and no brand matched.

Options:
  --facet <k=v>   Up to 20 explicit filters that override generated facets by name. Each needs 1..100 nonblank values of at most 256 characters. Product-only color, color_family, is_activewear and internal brand_quality_score are rejected.
  --limit <n>     Maximum number of matching brands. Default: 24. Minimum: 1. Maximum: 100.
  --like <brand>  Canonical source brands whose averaged embeddings guide the search.

Calls: searchBrandsFromText (through @octogen-ai/sdk 0.9.0)

Global options: storerouter --help
```

```text
storerouter brands similar <brand>… [--facet k=v]… [--exclude-facet k=v]… [--limit <n>]

  --limit <n>            Maximum number of similar brands. Default: 24. Minimum: 1. Maximum: 100.
```

## brands products

```text
storerouter brands products <brand> [--limit <n>] [--offset <n>]

  Browse one brand's products

  Products from the catalogs your key can access. Continue with --offset
  <nextOffset>; paging stops at offset 10000. A page can hold fewer than
  --limit products, or none, while more remain: follow nextOffset, not the count.

Options:
  --limit <n>   Limit Default: 24. Minimum: 1. Maximum: 100.
  --offset <n>  Rows to skip. Pagination stops at offset 10000: `hasMore` goes false there even when more rows exist. Default: 0. Minimum: 0. Maximum: 10000.

Calls: browseBrandProducts (through @octogen-ai/sdk 0.9.0)

Global options: storerouter --help
```

## resolve

```text
storerouter resolve --html <file|-> [--url <url>]

  Resolve a product from page HTML you already have

  Stateless: no index read, no outbound fetch, no caching. The answer comes
  entirely from the document you submit.

  HTML is never taken from an argument — the cap is 5 MiB and argv is the
  wrong channel for a payload that size, quite apart from what a
  multi-megabyte argv entry does to an agent transcript.

  Requires an API key.

Options:
  --html <file|->  Product page HTML to resolve. Capped at 5 MiB — the same bound the live on-demand fetch path enforces, so any page that path could retrieve is submittable here.
  --url <value>    Optional, but strongly recommended: the page's source URL, ideally location.href read at the same instant the DOM was serialized. It anchors relative image URLs and JSON-LD candidate selection exactly like the live path's final fetched URL, and it is echoed back as requestedUrl — on storefronts that record an in-page variant selection only in the URL's query parameters, this is the only variant-qualified identity the response retains. When absent the page itself must declare its canonical URL (JSON-LD Product/variant url, link rel=canonical, selected Offer.url, or og:url) or resolution fails with product_not_found.

Calls: resolveProductFromHtml (through @octogen-ai/sdk 0.9.0)

Global options: storerouter --help
```

## api

```text
storerouter api <METHOD> <path> [--data @file|-|<json>] [--query k=v]…

  Raw authenticated /v1 request (unstable by construction)

  UNSTABLE BY CONSTRUCTION: you own the request body. No request or response
  types, no defaults, and no promise the route exists — every other command
  names an operationId that is checked against the published contract, and
  this one takes the path from you.

  You still get key resolution, retry, rate-limit surfacing, the exit-code
  taxonomy, and redaction.

  This is how the eight coverage/url-lists operations stay reachable — their
  first-class CLI is `octogen-url-lists` in the Python SDK, whose mutations
  are dry-run-by-default behind --apply.

Options:
  --data <json|@file|->  Request body: inline JSON, @file, or - for stdin.
  --query <k=v>          Query parameter as k=v (repeatable).

Global options: storerouter --help
```
